overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance clearly demonstrates that speculative space scenarios and extreme planetary facts (especially 'What If' framing and bizarre weather/asset values on exoplanets) heavily outperform standard biology or generic history facts. Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' lead in views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view).

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical Planetary Immersion ('What If You Fell Into...')
winning_patterns.evidence: IYuce8vaU3Y ('What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?') generated 1,029 views and 38 likes quickly, showing exceptional engagement compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive, high-stakes hypothetical space scenarios involving extreme physical environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b') pulled 1,031 views and 36 likes, proving audiences love counter-intuitive cosmic realities.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on newly discovered or extreme exoplanets with bizarre physical properties like extreme absorption, bizarre rain, or impossible temperatures.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos like 2fqaGqfsR4A ('Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories') and Jc04LVKNd2s stagnated with under 20-50 views over extended periods.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize simple psychological listicles unless framed as high-stakes mystery or dramatic scenarios.

weak_patterns.evidence: yLm-FjYH6-k ('The 2,000-Year-Old Mystery Science Can't Solve') had low velocity and zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid vague historical mysteries without a concrete, visually compelling hook or interactive element.
